_note: One telephone story told by eight keepers. Each telling: when it was published, which night it sets the call on, the first count, the cause it gives, a short quotation and the raw file it is checked against by verify_sources.py. 'night' is what the telling itself says or, where marked 'inferred', what its cause or its notes point to. Assembled by hand from the sources; no model output is used as fact.

1979-11-09.label: 9 November 1979
1979-11-09.cause_text: an exercise tape fed into the live warning system
1979-11-09.press_note: Alert reported in the press on 11 November 1979 (Long After, E42); the call is not in it.

1980-06-03.label: 3 June 1980
1980-06-03.press_note: Alert reported in the press on 6 June 1980 (Long After, E44); the call is not in it.

tellings.keeper: Robert M. Gates, From the Shadows (Simon & Schuster), p. 114
tellings.quote: Someone had mistakenly put military exercise tapes into the computer system.
tellings.check_via: the passage as quoted in full by the National Security Archive (EBB 371); the book itself was not read

tellings.keeper: National Security Archive, Electronic Briefing Book 371 (W. Burr)
tellings.quote: took place in the middle of the night on 9 November 1979

tellings.keeper: Eric Schlosser, Command and Control (2013), endnotes to p. 368
tellings.night_how: inferred: the note for the 2,200 missiles cites Gates and is followed by the note for the defective chip; the main text was not read
tellings.quote: 2,200 missiles were heading toward the United States: See Gates, From the Shadows, p. 114

tellings.keeper: Chatham House, Too Close for Comfort (Lewis, Williams, Pelopidas, Aghlani)
tellings.quote: At 02:26 on 3 June 1980, National Security Advisor Zbigniew Brzezinski received a telephone call

tellings.keeper: Eric Schlosser, 'World War Three, by Mistake', The New Yorker
tellings.quote: Odom called back and offered a correction: twenty-two hundred Soviet missiles had been launched.

tellings.keeper: Daryl G. Kimball, 'Nuclear False Warnings and the Risk of Catastrophe', Arms Control Today
tellings.quote: false alarm caused by software simulating a Soviet missile attack

tellings.keeper: Wikipedia, 'List of nuclear close calls', as read on 2026-10-12
tellings.quote: NORAD computers then placed the number of incoming missiles at 2,200.

relay.offered: the Atelier, The Hinge (cycle 007, session 1): Wikipedia tells the call under 1979, Chatham House under 1980
relay.answer: confirmed, and traced: the call reaches the public record only in 1996, without a night; it was set on 1979 in 2012 and on 1980 from 2013 on, and one telling joins the 1980 night to the 1979 cause.
